section_caveats: Initial research using English-language sources incorrectly concluded that no Slovak-born woman who emigrated post-1993 met the criteria for inclusion. This was an artefact of English-language search bias, not a demographic reality. Slovak-language sources (slovaks.ai, startitup.sk, forbes.sk) surfaced multiple candidates. The section includes Kristina Cahojova (kegg, San Francisco) and Katarina Simkova (Google DeepMind, London). The broader pattern that emerged from research: Slovak talent that stayed in Slovakia built successful companies at home (ESET, Sygic, Innovatrics, Pixel Federation, Vacuumlabs, Slido). Those who left the V4 region tend to concentrate in AI/ML research and hardware/biotech rather than software-only ventures. The notable people in this section should be read alongside sections 1-3 which show the structural patterns these individual stories exemplify.

people.name: Andrej Karpathy
people.narrative: Left Slovakia at 15 when his family emigrated to Canada. Completed all higher education abroad: BSc in Toronto, MSc in Vancouver, PhD at Stanford under Fei-Fei Li. Built the deep learning course that trained a generation of AI engineers.
people.impact: Founding member of OpenAI, former Senior Director of AI at Tesla (Autopilot). One of the most influential AI educators globally through his Stanford CS231n course and YouTube channel.

people.name: Michal Valko
people.narrative: Completed MSc at Slovak University of Technology, then left for PhD at CMU and postdoc at INRIA France. Joined DeepMind in London where he leads reinforcement learning research.
people.impact: Senior Staff Research Scientist at Google DeepMind. Published 100+ papers in top ML venues. One of the most cited Slovak-born researchers in AI after Karpathy.

people.name: Andrej Babiš
people.narrative: Moved to Czechia around Slovak independence in 1993. Built Agrofert into one of Central Europe's largest conglomerates, then entered Czech politics. I do not support him, but his political and capital strength is sadly undoubtable. He represents how Slovak-born talent and capital flowed to Prague when the federation dissolved.
people.impact: Czech Republic's second-richest person. Former Prime Minister of Czechia (2017-2021). Current President of Czechia (2025-). His career illustrates how Bratislava-born capital chose Prague over staying.

people.name: Juraj Slafkovský
people.trigger: structural failure of Slovak youth development
people.narrative: Left Slovakia at 15 for TPS Turku in Finland because Slovak junior hockey infrastructure could not develop him further. Drafted 1st overall by Montreal Canadiens in 2022. Publicly criticized the systemic problems in Slovak hockey development.
people.impact: First Slovak #1 overall NHL draft pick. His departure and public criticism (The Athletic, Arpon Basu, Oct 2024) made visible what thousands of young Slovak athletes experience: leaving is the only path to elite development.

people.name: Kristina Cahojova
people.narrative: Completed university in Slovakia, won Napad Roku student entrepreneur award in 2013, then left for San Francisco. Founded Lady Technologies and built kegg, an FDA-registered fertility tracking device now used by over 100,000 customers globally.
people.impact: CEO of Lady Technologies (kegg). Grew the company to 90% year-over-year revenue growth. Launched in Japan, backed by SOSV. Represents the post-2010 wave of Slovak founders who bypassed Prague entirely for Silicon Valley.

people.name: Boris Kudlička
people.narrative: Graduated from VSMU Bratislava in stage design, immediately moved to Warsaw's Teatr Wielki in 1996. Became chief scenographer there by 2005. His work now spans Berlin Staatsoper, Washington and LA opera (with Placido Domingo), and major European houses.
people.impact: Gold Medal at Prague Quadrennial 2007. Works at the highest level of international opera production. Proves that Slovak artistic talent can reach global stages, but only by leaving entirely and building a career from scratch abroad.

people.name: Katarina Simkova
people.narrative: Studied computer science at FMFI Comenius University in Bratislava, then joined Google DeepMind in London as a Research Engineer. Part of the wave of Slovak CS graduates recruited directly by top international AI labs.
people.impact: Research Engineer at Google DeepMind. Represents the pipeline from Slovak university CS programs directly to world-leading AI labs, bypassing Slovak industry entirely.

people.name: Jana Košecká
people.trigger: PhD pursuit at top research university
people.narrative: Studied mathematics at Comenius University in Bratislava, then left for PhD at University of Pennsylvania in the early 1990s. Built her career in American academia, now a full professor at George Mason University specializing in visual navigation and scene understanding.
people.impact: Full Professor at George Mason University. Decades-long career in computer vision research. Co-author of a widely used robotics textbook. Represents the early 1990s wave of Slovak academics who left immediately after independence and never returned.

people.name: Ján Tkáč
people.narrative: Left at 25 for postdoctoral work, with stays at Linkoping and Lund in Sweden and at Oxford; the source register gives no dates or order for them. Has worked at the Institute of Chemistry of the Slovak Academy of Sciences since 2009. Won an ERC Starting Grant (ELENA, 2012 call) four years after returning, running 2013 to 2017, and built a glycomics research group there.
people.impact: The contrast case, though not the one it first appeared to be: the grant followed the return rather than causing it. ELENA brought an EU contribution of 1,155,970 EUR to the Institute of Chemistry SAV over 2013 to 2017.
